learning_outcomes.text: Perform the simulation of general-purpose electronic circuits with computer tools.
Analyze the operation of a wide variety of electronic circuits that use idealized operational amplifiers.
Synthesize filters with discrete elements, both passive and active (based on operational amplifiers).

Understand the functions of the different electronic sub-circuits (current sources and mirrors, differential stages, coupling stages, output stages and protections) that configure the internal structure of an operational amplifier.
Understand and quantify how the real internal structure of an operational amplifier modifies its idealized behavior.
Quantify how the real characteristics of an operational amplifier modify its behavior in circuits and establish comparisons with calculations obtained assuming ideal behavior.
Understand the operation of other general-purpose analog integrated circuits and their application in communications and power electronics.

syllabus_topics: Amplifiers in common emitter, common collector and common base configurations.
Amplifiers in common source and common drain configurations.
Effect of frequency on the transistor model.
Basic linear and non-linear circuits with ideal operational amplifiers.
Synthesis of filters with passive elements.

assessment_methods.method: Continuous evaluation (PL1) - attendance and performance in practical results

assessment_rules: The final grade for the theoretical block is calculated as: ((0.125 x EP1) + (0.175 x EP2) + (0.6 x EF1) + (0.1 x T)) x TG. The final grade for the practical block is calculated as: (0.5 x PL1) + (0.5 x PL2). The final grade for the ordinary call is calculated as: ((5 x Theory) + (Practices)) / 6. The practical block grade is retained for all calls within the same academic year and for the first extraordinary call of the following year. In case of doubt regarding authorship or unauthorized means, an in-person defense may be requested.
